bullets.title: NVDA: Strong beat & raise; FY28 rev growth guided to +75%; CEO search ongoing
bullets.body: NVDA Q3 revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y) beat consensus ~$109B by ~6%; EPS $2.68 vs $2.48 est; DC revenue $107.6B (+110% y/y). Q4 guided to $130B midpoint (~4% above street), FY28 raised to +75% y/y from +70%. Vera Rubin contributed ~$20B in its first full quarter (fastest ramp in company history); supply commitments rose to $390B from $279B; total commitments $518B. Board ruled out reinstating Jensen Huang; SEC civil probe opened; H200 shipments to China halted. Street broadly bullish (75% buy, avg PT ~$266) but bear cases center on CEO succession, C2028 demand visibility, and export controls — UBS cuts 2028E EPS to $18.80, lowers PT to $220; Wolfe cuts PT to $200; Jefferies cuts to $250; Citi raises CY27/28 ests, maintains Buy/$225; GS maintains Buy/$220; MS upgrades to $260; Summit Insights downgrades to Hold.

bullets.title: NVDA supply chain read-through: semis, memory, neoclouds broadly positive
bullets.body: NVDA's raised FY28 outlook and $100B+ incremental supply commits drive broad read-through for AI infrastructure names. Memory undersupply expected until Q2 2028 (HBM WPM capacity growing 390k→690k by end-2027); MU highlighted as key beneficiary as memory becomes the gating factor for agentic AI with RBC raising estimates. Neocloud operators ($32B commitments) see NVDA adopting a 'disciplined and selective' financing stance, a modest headwind at the margin. Hyperscaler capex tracking +104% y/y in CY27; cloud backlog rose to $2.5T from $2T.

bullets.title: CRDO: Patent dispute with MRVL settled; stock +3.7% pre-market
bullets.body: Credo Technology settled its patent dispute with Marvell Technology on confidential terms. CRDO traded +3.7% in pre-market. Separately, Morgan Stanley warns that the FCC's advancing ban on Chinese optical transceivers (60-65% of market today) could create AI datacenter bottlenecks and jeopardizes the LITE/MRVL deal requiring China regulatory approval.

bullets.title: APP: In talks to acquire Criteo (CRTO); rationale fits Consumer vertical strategy
bullets.body: AppLovin is reportedly among firms in acquisition talks for Criteo, with a potential deal before year-end per KeyBanc. CRTO valued at 2.3x 2028E EV/EBITDA vs a 3-year median of 3.3x; 2028E net revenue $1.11B, EBITDA $345M. JPM notes CRTO brings ~$4.6B annual media spend, ~17k clients, ~740M DAUs, and significant headcount reduction potential (Criteo has 3,504 employees vs. APP's 898), making APP the more probable acquirer over PE.

bullets.title: NYT: Citi downgrades to Neutral, cuts PT to $76 on eroding engagement metrics
bullets.body: Citi downgraded New York Times from Buy to Neutral and cut its price target from $85 to $76 (now only ~3% upside from ~$73.82). The downgrade cites falling app downloads, declining active users, worsening engagement frequency and time, falling organic web visits, and decelerating monetization as AI overviews reduce ad impressions. Analyst remains positive on long-term outlook but sees near-term trends foreshadowing slower topline growth.

bullets.title: SNOW & MDB: Multiple desks raising estimates ahead of upcoming earnings
bullets.body: Oppenheimer and Opco both raise FY28 estimates for SNOW ahead of Dec 2 earnings, expecting product growth >40% y/y, 126% NRR, and CoCo driving large-scale Teradata/Netezza migrations; UBS/Karl Keirstead reiterates Buy on AI lift to data spend. For MDB, desks expect ~4% Q3 revenue upside, Atlas NRR ~122%, and FY27 guidance raised to +24-25% from +21-23%; MDB also acquired Firebolt for real-time analytics integration.

bullets.title: MSFT: Ignite confirms broadening AI monetization; Citi reiterates Buy/$680
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on MSFT with $680 PT (34% upside) following Ignite, citing uptick in M365/Copilot Cowork activity, E7 enterprise deployment traction, and Fabric momentum. MSFT unveiled MAI-Code-2 (98% frontier performance at ~40% cost) and Decision-1.1 (10x faster, 200x cheaper than LLMs, 4,000+ customers). META's Muse agent is expanding to Azure; AWS Vera CPU partnership noted. Subscription-plus-usage monetization model seen as cracked.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini 4 Hydrogen with task automation rolls out; Waymo pulled from highways
bullets.body: Google rolled out Gemini 4 Hydrogen (agentic task features) to ~250M users — frictionless toggle vs META Muse's download requirement, and ~4x compute efficiency vs Gemini 3.8 Flash per MS. On the negative side, California DMV banned Waymo from state freeways after two incidents, prompting Alphabet to block Waymo vehicles from highways nationwide pending review. GOOGL +0.7% pre-market.

bullets.title: PANW: Setup into Q1 print — JPM expects NGS ARR beat needed to reignite stock
bullets.body: JPM highlights PANW is down ~25% from recent highs despite strong cyber demand. Street expects Q1 NGS Net New ARR ~$460M; JPM's internal expectation is ~$550M. Q2 guidance of +$400-450M NGS Net New ARR and a FY27 raise are seen as requirements for the stock to power higher. No rating change noted.

bullets.title: TEAM: Solid Q1 momentum; data center migrations driving business; FY27 upside potential
bullets.body: RBC notes TEAM delivered a solid Q1 with continuing momentum; data center migrations are a key driver and enterprise GTM maturation could unlock upside to FY27 estimates. Citi's KubeCon checks separately highlight enterprise stickiness to Jira and limited appetite for AI-native replacement tools.

bullets.title: NOW & RDDT: Positive conference color at RBC TIMT
bullets.body: RBC is bullish on NOW — well-positioned to monetize AI with FDEs unlocking broader adoption; growth and margin story becoming evident in 2027. RDDT: moving to logged-in model accelerates investor realization; product initiatives have ~12 months runway with contribution rate per user rising; time spent flagged as an incremental metric to watch.

bullets.title: HPE: Weak 4Q setup flagged; channel inventory at 15 weeks (2x normal)
bullets.body: Citi notes HPE expects 4Q revenues below seasonal with weak consumer PC demand and channel inventory at ~15 weeks, double normal levels. HPE reports this week (earnings calendar). Citi suggests buying HPE puts as an event-driven trade.

bullets.title: NET: Strong F2Q setup per Citi; AI/Fed tailwinds, cloud net adds +$12M vs +$10M prior
bullets.body: Citi's analyst expects Cloudflare to report a strong F2Q print driven by AI and Federal government tailwinds, with cloud net adds of +$12M versus +$10M in the prior quarter. No rating change noted.

bullets.title: NVDA valuation extreme: trading at 24-year low relative P/E vs S&P 500
bullets.body: MS Alpha note highlights NVDA's $2T market cap wipeout has pushed NTM P/E to ~10.6x (lowest in 13 years) and a 40% discount to SPX — the lowest relative P/E in 24 years vs. the 5-year avg of ~33x. MS maintains Overweight with $260 PT (67% upside), arguing multiple compression is largely behind the stock. Separately, hedge funds have been net selling Info Tech at the fastest 10-year pace (-4.4 z-score) over six weeks, with semis leading outflows.

bullets.title: MU: Supply tightening in 2027/28; memory becoming key Agentic AI gating factor
bullets.body: RBC raises MU estimates following NVDA's earnings, noting industry supply is expected to tighten in 2027/28 versus 2026 as AI demand accelerates. Memory is increasingly the bottleneck for agentic AI workloads; SCAs provide extended demand visibility. MU plans 100% excess cash return via buybacks. HBM capacity growing from 390k to 690k WPM by end-2027 per UBS.

bullets.title: DELL & HPE earnings on deck this week; AI server demand a key focus
bullets.body: DELL and HPE are both on the earnings calendar this week (Nov 18-25 per SA). Positive NVDA read-through on AI server demand is a tailwind, though HPE faces near-term channel inventory headwinds (~15 weeks, 2x normal per Citi). SMCI, CRWV, and neocloud operators also benefit from NVDA's raised FY28 outlook.

bullets.title: INTU: On earnings calendar this week
bullets.body: Intuit is on the earnings calendar for the Nov 18-25 window per SA's earnings calendar. No pre-earnings research views flagged in this digest window.

bullets.title: APP/CRTO M&A: Optical transceiver ban could complicate LITE/MRVL deal
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley warns the FCC's advancing ban on Chinese optical transceivers (60-65% of market) would eliminate a key demand channel for LITE (60-65% of production assembled in China) and that the LITE/MRVL merger requires China regulatory approval — seen as less likely if a full ban is implemented. MS prefers a ban at the 3.2T threshold over a full ban given hyperscaler opposition and AI deployment delay risk.

bullets.title: NKE: GS flags elevated execution risk; FY28 EPS expected to decline Y/Y post Investor Day
bullets.body: Nike's Investor Day saw a 13% intraday range (opened +7%, closed -6%). GS notes guidance is heavily back-half weighted with FY28 EPS expected to decline y/y, below prior FactSet consensus, as the company targets margin recovery in FY29-31 at the high end of historical ranges contingent on significant inflection. Initial investor feedback was immediate skepticism; GS notes NKE RSI at ~40 and says investors will likely demand further execution comfort before turning constructive.

bullets.title: BABA: NVDA allegedly introduced Alibaba to alleged chip-smuggling spy pre-2022 export controls
bullets.body: The Information reports Nvidia introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang, allegedly linked to a Chinese chip-smuggling scandal, shortly before US semiconductor export controls took effect in 2022. Former Nvidia sales chief is cited as the connection. This is an incremental headline risk for both NVDA and BABA given ongoing regulatory and export control scrutiny.
